+# RFD 0001 - Job Worker Service (Linux)
+
+## Required Approvers
+* Interview Panel: `espadolini` `nklaassen` `r0mant`
+
+## What
+A prototype job worker service providing a gRPC API for remote execution of isolated Linux processes with real-time log streaming.
+
+## Why
+This service provides a secure, resource-constrained environment for executing arbitrary payloads, serving as a foundation for distributed task scheduling.
+## Details
+
+### User Experience and CLI Interfaces
+
+The `worker-cli` acts as the primary entry point. Output is designed to be machine-readable where possible while maintaining human-centric status updates.
+
+**Start a job**
+User starts a long-running process with resource limits.
+```bash
+$ worker-cli start --cmd "/bin/sh -c 'while true; do echo hello; sleep 1; done'" --mem-limit 100MB --cpu-limit 50
+> [2026-01-21T14:00:01Z] Job started: 1234-5678-90ab
+```
+
+**Query status (Running Job)**
+User queries the status of a job. 
+```bash
+$ worker-cli status 1234-5678-90ab
+Job: 1234-5678-90ab
+Status: Running
+```
+
+**Stream output (Running Job)**
+User streams the output of a job.
+```bash
+$ worker-cli stream 1234-5678-90ab
+Job: 1234-5678-90ab
+Status: Running
+Command: /bin/sh -c 'while true; do echo hello; sleep 1; done'
+Args:  --mem-limit 100MB --cpu-limit 50
+> [2026-01-21T14:00:01Z] Job started: 1234-5678-90ab
+> [2026-01-21T14:00:01Z] hello
+> [2026-01-21T14:00:02Z] hello
+> [2026-01-21T14:00:03Z] hello
+> ^C
+```
+
+**Stop a job**
+User terminates the job.
+```bash
+$ worker-cli stop 1234-5678-90ab
+> Job stopped.
+```
+
+**Stream output (Stopped Job)**
+User streams the output of a job.
+```bash
+$ worker-cli stream 1234-5678-90ab
+Job: 1234-5678-90ab
+Status: Stopped
+Command: /bin/sh -c 'while true; do echo hello; sleep 1; done'
+Args:  --mem-limit 100MB --cpu-limit 50

+> [2026-01-21T14:00:02Z] hello
+> [2026-01-21T14:00:03Z] hello
+> [2026-01-21T14:00:04Z] hello
+> [2026-01-21T14:00:05Z] hello

+Exit Code: 0
+Job stopped.
+Status Changed: Stopped
+```

+The system consists of three main components:
+1.  **Worker Library**: A low-level wrapper around `os/exec` and `syscall`. It manages the process lifecycle, namespace isolation, and Cgroup attachment.
+      * Remote Process Execution: [os/exec](https://pkg.go.dev/os/exec)
+      * Resource Isolation: [sys/unix](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/sys/unix)

+          end

+          NS[[Namespaces]]
+      end
+    end

+    MAP --> B2

+    SVR --> P2

+```mermaid

+    autonumber
+    participant C as CLI
+    participant S as gRPC Server
+    participant L as Library
+    participant K as Linux Kernel
+
+    Note over C, K: StartRequest() Sequence
+    C->>S: StartRequest()
+    S->>S: Authenticate()
+    S->>L: InitJob(Specs, Limits)
+    L->>K: mkdir /sys/fs/cgroup/job-123
+    L->>K: write memory.max, cpu.max
+    L->>K: fork() with CLONE_NEW*
+    K-->>L: Return PID
+    L->>K: write PID to cgroup.procs
+    L-->>S: Return Job ID
+    S-->>C: StartResponse (Job ID: 123)
+
+    Note over C, K: StreamRequest() Sequence
+    C->>S: StreamRequest(Job ID: 123)
+    S->>L: Subscribe to OutputBuffer
+    L->>C: Replay historical bytes
+    
+    loop Real-time Tail
+        K->>L: Stdout/Stderr data
+        L->>L: Append to buffer & Broadcast()
+        L->>C: LogChunk (Live)
+    end

+      * gRPC Library: [grpc](https://pkg.go.dev/google.golang.org/grpc)
+3.  **CLI**: A Cobra-based implementation that manages the mTLS handshake and renders gRPC stream chunks to the local TTY.
+      * CLI Library: [cobra](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/spf13/cobra)
+
+#### Architecture Diagram
+```mermaid
+graph TD
+    subgraph "Client"
+        C1[CLI A]

+    end

+    subgraph "Server"
+        SVR[gRPC Server]

+        B1[OutputBuffer]
+        B2[OutputBuffer]
+
+        subgraph "Linux Kernel"
+          subgraph "Job 1 Sandbox"
+              P1((Process 1))
+          end
+          
+          subgraph "Job 2 Sandbox"
+              P2((Process 2))
+          end
+
+          CG[[Cgroups v2]]
+          NS[[Namespaces]]
+      end
+    end
+
+    %% Flow
+    C1 -- "Job 1 (Stream)" --> SVR
+    C2 -- "Job 2 (Start)" --> SVR
+    SVR <--> MAP
+
+    MAP --> B1
+    MAP --> B2
+    
+    SVR --> P1
+    SVR --> P2
+

+    P2 -.-> B2 -.-> SVR

+    P1 & P2 --- NS

+
+#### Start and Stream Sequence Diagram
+```mermaid
+sequenceDiagram
+    autonumber
+    participant C as CLI
+    participant S as gRPC Server
+    participant L as Library
+    participant K as Linux Kernel

+    C->>S: StartRequest()
+    S->>S: Authenticate()

+    L->>K: mkdir /sys/fs/cgroup/job-123

+### Implementation
+#### Process Orchestration
+We will utilize `os/exec.Cmd` while overriding `SysProcAttr` to handle kernel-level isolation.
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***Isolation***: Processes are spawned into new namespaces (PID, UTS, Network) using `CLONE_NEW*` flags to prevent host-level lateral movement. 
+        * *NOTE: Creating a new Network namespace will disallow networking calls. Future work might include adding back networking capabilities while taking advantage of the current sandboxing of each process.*
+  *  ***Resource Constraints***: We will leverage Cgroups v2. Upon job initiation, the library creates a unique Cgroup leaf node at `/sys/fs/cgroup/worker/<job_id>/`. Limits are written to memory.max and cpu.max before the process is migrated into the group to ensure each process is resource constrained before fork() is called.
+  *  ***Process Tree Termination***: To prevent orphaned processes, the library will set the process group ID `Setpgid: true`. That means that on `Stop()`, a `SIGKILL` is sent to the negative PID (e.g., -1234) to terminate the entire process group.
+
+##### Start Process Example
+```go
+func (j *Job) Start() error {
+    // 1. Create the Cgroup leaf node & apply limits
+    cgroupPath := "/sys/fs/cgroup/worker/" + j.ID
+    os.MkdirAll(cgroupPath, 0755)
+    os.WriteFile(cgroupPath+"/memory.max", []byte(j.LimitBytes), 0644)
+
+    // 2. Prepare command with Namespace isolation (PID, NET, UTS)
+    j.Cmd = exec.Command(j.Command, j.Args...)
+    j.Cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{
+        Cloneflags: syscall.CLONE_NEWPID | syscall.CLONE_NEWNET | syscall.CLONE_NEWUTS,
+        Pdeathsig:  syscall.SIGKILL, // Kill job if worker server dies
+    }
+
+    // 3. Launch process and immediately attach to Cgroup
+    j.Cmd.Start()
+    // TODO: Note that there is a small race window where the process runs outside the cgroup. 
+    // A more robust solution would involve a fork/exec model where the child process adds itself to the cgroup before executing the target binary.
+    os.WriteFile(cgroupPath+"/cgroup.procs", []byte(strconv.itoa(j.Cmd.Process.Pid)), 0644)
+
+    return nil
+}
+```
+
+#### Output Streaming & Broadcasting 
+The `OutputBuffer` is implemented as a synchronized, in-memory store.
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***Replay***: Each `Job` maintains a maintains a byte slice of all historical output. New gRPC callers first read the existing buffer from their current offset.
+  *  ***Signaling***: We use `sync.Cond` for the broadcasting layer. When the library reads a chunk from the process pipes, it appends to the buffer and triggers `Broadcast()`, waking all dormant gRPC stream goroutines.
+
+##### Process Capture Stdout/Stderr to OutputBuffer Example
+```go
+func (b *OutputBuffer) Capture(source io.Reader) {
+    scanner := bufio.NewScanner(source)
+    for scanner.Scan() {
+        b.Lock()
+        // 1. Append to the "Replay" history
+        b.data = append(b.data, scanner.Bytes()...)
+        b.data = append(b.data, '\n')
+        b.Unlock()
+
+        // 2. "Broadcast" to all sleeping gRPC goroutines
+        b.L.Lock()
+        b.Broadcast()
+        b.L.Unlock()
+    }
+}
+```
+
+#### Security & Identity
+Security and Identity are paramount to protecting our servers from malicious actors. The following requirements ensure we protect the server:
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***mTLS 1.3***: Mandatory mutual TLS using a shared internal CA. We explicitly restrict the server to `TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384` to ensure modern cipher parity.
+  *  ***Identity-Based Auth***: The server extracts the `Subject.CommonName` (CN) from the client certificate. This CN is treated as the "OwnerID." Any request to `Stop`, `Status`, or `Stream` a job is rejected if the caller's CN does not match the job's `ExecutionSpecs.OwnerCommonName`.
+  *  ***Attack Surface Reduction***: The worker runs as a non-privileged user where possible, utilizing `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` only where required for Cgroup/Namespace setup.
+
+##### Verify Certificate Example
+```go
+func (s *workerServer) Authorize(ctx context.Context, jobID string) error {
+    // 1. Extract Peer info from gRPC context
+    p, _ := peer.FromContext(ctx)
+    tlsInfo := p.AuthInfo.(credentials.TLSInfo)
+    
+    // 2. Extract Common Name (CN) from the client certificate
+    clientCN := tlsInfo.State.PeerCertificates[0].Subject.CommonName
+    
+    // 3. Verify Ownership: Only the creator can manage the job
+    job := s.store.Get(jobID)
+    if job.OwnerCommonName != clientCN {
+        return status.Error(codes.PermissionDenied, "Identity mismatch")
+    }
+    
+    return nil
+}
+```
+
+#### Server Consideration
+Since the Server itself will be serving concurrent traffic with many clients, inflight goroutines should be sandboxed as well. We will need to consider graceful shutdowns and error handling to accommodate.
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***Graceful Shutdown***: If the server is shutdown or exits unexpectedly, we would like the server to gracefully shutdown. That means we'd like to handle each job and tell them to stop and let connected clients exit as well.
+  *  ***Error Handling***: Each `Job` will have a panic handler that will gracefully log errors to a channel before letting each process goroutine safely exit.
+
+
+##### Graceful Shutdown Example
+```go
+func (s *workerServer) GracefulShutdown(grpcServer *grpc.Server) {
+    // 1. Listen for OS termination signals (SIGINT, SIGTERM)
+    stop := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
+    signal.Notify(stop, os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
+    <-stop // Block until a signal is received
+
+    log.Println("Shutdown signal received. Cleaning up jobs...")
+
+    // 2. Stop the gRPC server from accepting new connections
+    grpcServer.GracefulStop()
+
+    // 3. Cleanup active jobs
+    s.mu.RLock()
+    defer s.mu.RUnlock()
+    for id, job := range s.jobs {
+        log.Printf("Terminating job %s...", id)
+        job.Stop() // This should trigger the SIGKILL to the process group
+    }
+
+    log.Println("Shutdown complete.")
+}
+```
+
+##### Panic Handler Example
+```go
+func (s *workerServer) HandlePanic(jobID string) {
+    if r := recover(); r != nil {
+        // 1. Log the error with stack trace for debugging
+        log.Printf("[PANIC] Job %s crashed: %v\nStack: %s", jobID, r, debug.Stack())
+
+        // 2. Mark the job state as failed so the client knows what happened
+        s.mu.Lock()
+        if job, ok := s.jobs[jobID]; ok {
+            job.State.Status = StatusFailed
+            job.State.EndTime = time.Now().UTC()
+        }
+        s.mu.Unlock()
+
+        // 3. (Optional) Send a specific error chunk to any active gRPC streamers
+    }
+}
+
+// Example usage in the orchestration:
+go func() {
+    defer s.HandlePanic(job.ID)
+    s.streamOutput(job)
+}()
+```
+
+### Library Structs
+The bulk of the data that will be kept in memory will be in the `Job` struct. Each job will have a status, as well as other pieces of metadata like ID, job commands and arguments.
+```go
+// Job is the container for each process initiated by a client.
+// It contains the metadata for the Command, Process, and Lifecycle. It also provides access to the Log Stream buffer.
+type Job struct {
+	sync.RWMutex
+
+	// ID is a unique UUID generated for the job, distinct from the OS PID. This is the same ID the client will be provided to manage processes
+	ID string
+	// Specs holds the command from the client
+	Specs ExecutionSpecs
+	// Proc holds live handles to the running process.
+	Proc ProcessHandle
+	// State tracks the current status and timing of the job.
+	State Lifecycle
+	// Limit defines the resource boundaries for the process on the linux system.
+	Limit ResourceLimits
+	// Stream manages the in-memory buffer for replayable output.
+	Stream *OutputBuffer
+}
+
+// OutputBuffer implements a thread-safe, multi-consumer broadcaster for process output
+type OutputBuffer struct {
+	sync.RWMutex
+	// cond is a condition variable used to wake up dormant client streamers when new data arrives.
+	sync.Cond
+
+	// data is the in-memory store of all stdout/stderr produced by the process.
+	data []byte
+	// closed indicates the process has finished writing to the buffer.
+	closed bool
+
+}
+```
+
+#### Subtypes
+```go
+// JobStatus represents the current lifecycle state of a worker job.
+type JobStatus string
+
+const (
+	// StatusRunning indicates the process has started and is currently active.
+	StatusRunning JobStatus = "running"
+	// StatusStopped indicates the process was manually terminated by a user request.
+	StatusStopped JobStatus = "stopped"
+	// StatusCompleted indicates the process exited on its own with a zero exit code.
+	StatusCompleted JobStatus = "completed"
+	// StatusFailed indicates the process exited with a non-zero exit code or system error.
+	StatusFailed JobStatus = "failed"
+)
+
+// ExecutionSpecs defines the parameters provided by the client when a job is first created.
+type ExecutionSpecs struct {
+	// Command is the path to the executable to be run.
+	Command string
+	// Args is the list of arguments passed to the Command.
+	Args []string
+	// OwnerCommonName is the Common Name extracted from the client's TLS certificate, used for ownership-based authorization.
+	OwnerCommonName string
+}
+
+// ResourceLimits defines the kernel-level constraints applied to a job.
+// These are implemented via Cgroups on Linux.
+type ResourceLimits struct {
+	// MemoryLimitBytes is the maximum physical memory the process tree can consume.
+	MemoryLimitBytes int64
+	// CPULimitPercent is the maximum CPU usage allowed (e.g., 0.5 for 50% of a core).
+	CPULimitPercent float64
+}

+      * Resource Isolation: [sys/unix](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/sys/unix)

+#### Process Orchestration
+We will utilize `os/exec.Cmd` while overriding `SysProcAttr` to handle kernel-level isolation.
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***Isolation***: Processes are spawned into new namespaces (PID, UTS, Network) using `CLONE_NEW*` flags to prevent host-level lateral movement. 
+        * *NOTE: Creating a new Network namespace will disallow networking calls. Future work might include adding back networking capabilities while taking advantage of the current sandboxing of each process.*
+  *  ***Resource Constraints***: We will leverage Cgroups v2. Upon job initiation, the library creates a unique Cgroup leaf node at `/sys/fs/cgroup/worker/<job_id>/`. +        b.data = append(b.data, '\n')
+        b.Unlock()

+        b.Broadcast()
+        b.L.Unlock()
+    }

+> [2026-01-21T14:00:02Z] hello
+> [2026-01-21T14:00:03Z] hello
+> [2026-01-21T14:00:04Z] hello
+> [2026-01-21T14:00:05Z] hello
+Action: Stop
+Exit Code: 0
+Job stopped.
+Status Changed: Stopped
+```
+
+**Query status**
+User queries the status of a job (Stopped Job). 
+```bash
+$ worker-cli status 1234-5678-90ab
+Job: 1234-5678-90ab
+Status: stopped
+Exit Code: 0
+```
+
+### Architecture and Subsystems
+The system consists of three main components:
+1.  **Worker Library**: A low-level wrapper around `os/exec` and `syscall`. It manages the process lifecycle, namespace isolation, and Cgroup attachment.
+      * Remote Process Execution: [os/exec](https://pkg.go.dev/os/exec)
+      * Resource Isolation: [sys/unix](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/sys/unix)
+      * Process Output Streaming: Use internal `OutputBuffer` struct that will handle async read/writes from the Client and Processes. 
+2.  **gRPC Server**: An API layer to access the Worker Library. It handles mTLS termination, identity extraction from certificates, and maps gRPC streams to the library’s internal broadcasters.
+      * gRPC Library: [grpc](https://pkg.go.dev/google.golang.org/grpc)
+3.  **CLI**: A Cobra-based implementation that manages the mTLS handshake and renders gRPC stream chunks to the local TTY.
+      * CLI Library: [cobra](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/spf13/cobra)
+
+#### Architecture Diagram
+```mermaid
+graph TD
+    subgraph "Client"
+        C1[CLI A]
+        C2[CLI B]
+    end
+
+    subgraph "Server"
+        SVR[gRPC Server]
+        MAP[(Jobs Map)]
+        B1[OutputBuffer]
+        B2[OutputBuffer]
+
+        subgraph "Linux Kernel"
+          subgraph "Job 1 Sandbox"
+              P1((Process 1))
+          end
+          
+          subgraph "Job 2 Sandbox"
+              P2((Process 2))
+          end
+
+          CG[[Cgroups v2]]
+          NS[[Namespaces]]
+      end
+    end
+
+    %% Flow
+    C1 -- "Job 1 (Stream)" --> SVR
+    C2 -- "Job 2 (Start)" --> SVR
+    SVR <--> MAP
+
+    MAP --> B1
+    MAP --> B2
+    
+    SVR --> P1
+    SVR --> P2
+
+    P1 -.-> B1 -.-> SVR
+    P2 -.-> B2 -.-> SVR
+
+    P1 & P2 --- CG
+    P1 & P2 --- NS
+```
+
+#### Start and Stream Sequence Diagram
+```mermaid
+sequenceDiagram
+    autonumber
+    participant C as CLI
+    participant S as gRPC Server
+    participant L as Library
+    participant K as Linux Kernel
+
+    Note over C, K: StartRequest() Sequence
+    C->>S: StartRequest()
+    S->>S: Authenticate()
+    S->>L: InitJob(Specs, Limits)
+    L->>K: mkdir /sys/fs/cgroup/job-123
+    L->>K: write memory.max, cpu.max
+    L->>K: fork() with CLONE_NEW*
+    K-->>L: Return PID
+    L->>K: write PID to cgroup.procs
+    L-->>S: Return Job ID
+    S-->>C: StartResponse (Job ID: 123)
+
+    Note over C, K: StreamRequest() Sequence
+    C->>S: StreamRequest(Job ID: 123)
+    S->>L: Subscribe to OutputBuffer
+    L->>C: Replay historical bytes
+    
+    loop Real-time Tail
+        K->>L: Stdout/Stderr data
+        L->>L: Append to buffer & Broadcast()
+        L->>C: LogChunk (Live)
+    end
+```
+
+### Implementation
+#### Process Orchestration
+We will utilize `os/exec.Cmd` while overriding `SysProcAttr` to handle kernel-level isolation.
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***Isolation***: Processes are spawned into new namespaces (PID, UTS, Network) using `CLONE_NEW*` flags to prevent host-level lateral movement. 
+        * *NOTE: Creating a new Network namespace will disallow networking calls. Future work might include adding back networking capabilities while taking advantage of the current sandboxing of each process.*
+  *  ***Resource Constraints***: We will leverage Cgroups v2. Upon job initiation, the library creates a unique Cgroup leaf node at `/sys/fs/cgroup/worker/<job_id>/`. Limits are written to memory.max and cpu.max before the process is migrated into the group to ensure each process is resource constrained before fork() is called.
+  *  ***Process Tree Termination***: To prevent orphaned processes, the library will set the process group ID `Setpgid: true`. That means that on `Stop()`, a `SIGKILL` is sent to the negative PID (e.g., -1234) to terminate the entire process group.
+
+##### Start Process Example
+```go
+func (j *Job) Start() error {
+    // 1. Create the Cgroup leaf node & apply limits
+    cgroupPath := "/sys/fs/cgroup/worker/" + j.ID
+    os.MkdirAll(cgroupPath, 0755)
+    os.WriteFile(cgroupPath+"/memory.max", []byte(j.LimitBytes), 0644)
+
+    // 2. Prepare command with Namespace isolation (PID, NET, UTS)
+    j.Cmd = exec.Command(j.Command, j.Args...)
+    j.Cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{
+        Cloneflags: syscall.CLONE_NEWPID | syscall.CLONE_NEWNET | syscall.CLONE_NEWUTS,
+        Pdeathsig:  syscall.SIGKILL, // Kill job if worker server dies
+    }
+
+    // 3. Launch process and immediately attach to Cgroup
+    j.Cmd.Start()
+    // TODO: Note that there is a small race window where the process runs outside the cgroup. 
+    // A more robust solution would involve a fork/exec model where the child process adds itself to the cgroup before executing the target binary.
+    os.WriteFile(cgroupPath+"/cgroup.procs", []byte(strconv.itoa(j.Cmd.Process.Pid)), 0644)
+
+    return nil
+}
+```
+
+#### Output Streaming & Broadcasting 
+The `OutputBuffer` is implemented as a synchronized, in-memory store.
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***Replay***: Each `Job` maintains a maintains a byte slice of all historical output. New gRPC callers first read the existing buffer from their current offset.
+  *  ***Signaling***: We use `sync.Cond` for the broadcasting layer. When the library reads a chunk from the process pipes, it appends to the buffer and triggers `Broadcast()`, waking all dormant gRPC stream goroutines.
+
+##### Process Capture Stdout/Stderr to OutputBuffer Example
+```go
+func (b *OutputBuffer) Capture(source io.Reader) {
+    scanner := bufio.NewScanner(source)
+    for scanner.Scan() {
+        b.Lock()
+        // 1. Append to the "Replay" history
+        b.data = append(b.data, scanner.Bytes()...)
+        b.data = append(b.data, '\n')
+        b.Unlock()
+
+        // 2. "Broadcast" to all sleeping gRPC goroutines
+        b.L.Lock()
+        b.Broadcast()
+        b.L.Unlock()
+    }
+}
+```
+
+#### Security & Identity
+Security and Identity are paramount to protecting our servers from malicious actors. The following requirements ensure we protect the server:
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***mTLS 1.3***: Mandatory mutual TLS using a shared internal CA. We explicitly restrict the server to `TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384` to ensure modern cipher parity.
+  *  ***Identity-Based Auth***: The server extracts the `Subject.CommonName` (CN) from the client certificate. This CN is treated as the "OwnerID." Any request to `Stop`, `Status`, or `Stream` a job is rejected if the caller's CN does not match the job's `ExecutionSpecs.OwnerCommonName`.
+  *  ***Attack Surface Reduction***: The worker runs as a non-privileged user where possible, utilizing `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` only where required for Cgroup/Namespace setup.
+
+##### Verify Certificate Example
+```go
+func (s *workerServer) Authorize(ctx context.Context, jobID string) error {
+    // 1. Extract Peer info from gRPC context
+    p, _ := peer.FromContext(ctx)
+    tlsInfo := p.AuthInfo.(credentials.TLSInfo)
+    
+    // 2. Extract Common Name (CN) from the client certificate
+    clientCN := tlsInfo.State.PeerCertificates[0].Subject.CommonName
+    
+    // 3. Verify Ownership: Only the creator can manage the job
+    job := s.store.Get(jobID)
+    if job.OwnerCommonName != clientCN {
+        return status.Error(codes.PermissionDenied, "Identity mismatch")
+    }
+    
+    return nil
+}
+```
+
+#### Server Consideration
+Since the Server itself will be serving concurrent traffic with many clients, inflight goroutines should be sandboxed as well. We will need to consider graceful shutdowns and error handling to accommodate.
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***Graceful Shutdown***: If the server is shutdown or exits unexpectedly, we would like the server to gracefully shutdown. That means we'd like to handle each job and tell them to stop and let connected clients exit as well.
+  *  ***Error Handling***: Each `Job` will have a panic handler that will gracefully log errors to a channel before letting each process goroutine safely exit.
+
+
+##### Graceful Shutdown Example
+```go
+func (s *workerServer) GracefulShutdown(grpcServer *grpc.Server) {
+    // 1. Listen for OS termination signals (SIGINT, SIGTERM)
+    stop := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
+    signal.Notify(stop, os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
+    <-stop // Block until a signal is received
+
+    log.Println("Shutdown signal received. Cleaning up jobs...")
+
+    // 2. Stop the gRPC server from accepting new connections
+    grpcServer.GracefulStop()
+
+    // 3. Cleanup active jobs
+    s.mu.RLock()
+    defer s.mu.RUnlock()
+    for id, job := range s.jobs {
+        log.Printf("Terminating job %s...", id)
+        job.Stop() // This should trigger the SIGKILL to the process group
+    }
+
+    log.Println("Shutdown complete.")
+}
+```
+
+##### Panic Handler Example
+```go
+func (s *workerServer) HandlePanic(jobID string) {
+    if r := recover(); r != nil {
+        // 1. Log the error with stack trace for debugging
+        log.Printf("[PANIC] Job %s crashed: %v\nStack: %s", jobID, r, debug.Stack())
+
+        // 2. Mark the job state as failed so the client knows what happened
+        s.mu.Lock()
+        if job, ok := s.jobs[jobID]; ok {
+            job.State.Status = StatusFailed
+            job.State.EndTime = time.Now().UTC()
+        }
+        s.mu.Unlock()
+
+        // 3. (Optional) Send a specific error chunk to any active gRPC streamers
+    }
+}
+
+// Example usage in the orchestration:
+go func() {
+    defer s.HandlePanic(job.ID)
+    s.streamOutput(job)
+}()
+```
+
+### Library Structs
+The bulk of the data that will be kept in memory will be in the `Job` struct. Each job will have a status, as well as other pieces of metadata like ID, job commands and arguments.
+```go
+// Job is the container for each process initiated by a client.
+// It contains the metadata for the Command, Process, and Lifecycle. It also provides access to the Log Stream buffer.
+type Job struct {
+	sync.RWMutex
+
+	// ID is a unique UUID generated for the job, distinct from the OS PID. This is the same ID the client will be provided to manage processes
+	ID string
+	// Specs holds the command from the client
+	Specs ExecutionSpecs
+	// Proc holds live handles to the running process.
+	Proc ProcessHandle
+	// State tracks the current status and timing of the job.
+	State Lifecycle
+	// Limit defines the resource boundaries for the process on the linux system.
+	Limit ResourceLimits
+	// Stream manages the in-memory buffer for replayable output.
+	Stream *OutputBuffer
+}
+
+// OutputBuffer implements a thread-safe, multi-consumer broadcaster for process output
+type OutputBuffer struct {
+	sync.RWMutex
+	// cond is a condition variable used to wake up dormant client streamers when new data arrives.
+	sync.Cond
+
+	// data is the in-memory store of all stdout/stderr produced by the process.
+	data []byte
+	// closed indicates the process has finished writing to the buffer.
+	closed bool
+
+}
+```
+
+#### Subtypes
+```go
+// JobStatus represents the current lifecycle state of a worker job.
+type JobStatus string
+
+const (
+	// StatusRunning indicates the process has started and is currently active.
+	StatusRunning JobStatus = "running"
+	// StatusStopped indicates the process was manually terminated by a user request.
+	StatusStopped JobStatus = "stopped"
+	// StatusCompleted indicates the process exited on its own with a zero exit code.
+	StatusCompleted JobStatus = "completed"
+	// StatusFailed indicates the process exited with a non-zero exit code or system error.
+	StatusFailed JobStatus = "failed"
+)
+
+// ExecutionSpecs defines the parameters provided by the client when a job is first created.
+type ExecutionSpecs struct {
+	// Command is the path to the executable to be run.
+	Command string
+	// Args is the list of arguments passed to the Command.
+	Args []string
+	// OwnerCommonName is the Common Name extracted from the client's TLS certificate, used for ownership-based authorization.
+	OwnerCommonName string
+}
+
+// ResourceLimits defines the kernel-level constraints applied to a job.
+// These are implemented via Cgroups on Linux.
+type ResourceLimits struct {
+	// MemoryLimitBytes is the maximum physical memory the process tree can consume.
+	MemoryLimitBytes int64
+	// CPULimitPercent is the maximum CPU usage allowed (e.g., 0.5 for 50% of a core).
+	CPULimitPercent float64
+}
+
+// ProcessHandle maintains the live OS-level handles and controls for the process.
+type ProcessHandle struct {
+	// PID is the Operating System's Process ID.
+	PID int
+	// cmd is the underlying Go exec.Cmd instance managing the lifecycle.
+	cmd *exec.Cmd
+	// cancel is the context cancellation function used to signal a stop.
+	cancel context.CancelFunc
+}
+
+// Lifecycle tracks the temporal state and exit results of a job.
+type Lifecycle struct {
+	// Status is the current machine-state of the job.
+	Status JobStatus
+	// ExitCode is the exit code returned by the process upon termination.
+	ExitCode int
+	// StartTime is the UTC timestamp when the process was successfully started.
+	StartTime time.Time
+	// EndTime is the UTC timestamp when the process was ended.
+	EndTime time.Time
+}
+```
+
+
+
+### Client <> Server gRPC Specification
+The client to server schema will be using protobuf to support a standard gRPC API. The Start/Stop/Status apis will support synchronous job management, while Stream will return a stream of logs until the client wants to stop listening.
+
+#### Service Definition
+```protobuf
+service JobWorker {
+  rpc Start(StartRequest) returns (StartResponse);
+  rpc Stop(StopRequest) returns (StopResponse);
+  rpc Status(StatusRequest) returns (StatusResponse);
+  // Returns a stream that replays history and broadcasts new updates
+  rpc Stream(StreamRequest) returns (stream LogChunk);
+}
+```
+
+#### Start Job
+```protobuf
+message ResourceLimits {
+  uint64 memory_bytes = 1;
+  float cpu_max_percent = 2; // e.g., 50.0 for 50% of CPU time.
+}
+
+message StartRequest {
+  string command = 1;
+  repeated string args = 2;
+  ResourceLimits limits = 3;
+}
+
+message StartResponse {
+  string job_id = 1;
+}
+```
+
+#### Stop Job
+```protobuf
+message StopRequest {
+  string job_id = 1;
+}
+
+message StopResponse {}
+```
+
+#### Get Status
+```protobuf
+message StatusRequest {
+  string job_id = 1;
+}
+
+message StatusResponse {
+  string job_id = 1;
+  string state = 2;
+  int32 exit_code = 3;
+  // Added to match UX requirements
+  string command = 4;
+  repeated string args = 5;
+  google.protobuf.Timestamp started_at = 6;
+  google.protobuf.Timestamp ended_at = 7;
+}
+```
+
+#### Stream Job
+```protobuf
+message StreamRequest {
+  string job_id = 1;
+}
+
+message LogChunk {
+  bytes data = 1;
+  // Distinguishes between output streams
+  enum Source {
+    STDOUT = 0;

+        L->>L: Append to buffer & Broadcast()

+### Implementation
+#### Process Orchestration
+We will utilize `os/exec.Cmd` while overriding `SysProcAttr` to handle kernel-level isolation.
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***Isolation***: Processes are spawned into new namespaces (PID, UTS, Network) using `CLONE_NEW*` flags to prevent host-level lateral movement. 
+        * *NOTE: Creating a new Network namespace will disallow networking calls. Future work might include adding back networking capabilities while taking advantage of the current sandboxing of each process.*
+  *  ***Resource Constraints***: We will leverage Cgroups v2. Upon job initiation, the library creates a unique Cgroup leaf node at `/sys/fs/cgroup/worker/<job_id>/`. Limits are written to memory.max and cpu.max before the process is migrated into the group to ensure each process is resource constrained before fork() is called.
+  *  ***Process Tree Termination***: To prevent orphaned processes, the library will set the process group ID `Setpgid: true`. That means that on `Stop()`, a `SIGKILL` is sent to the negative PID (e.g., -1234) to terminate the entire process group.

+##### Start Process Example
+```go
+func (j *Job) Start() error {
+    // 1. Create the Cgroup leaf node & apply limits
+    cgroupPath := "/sys/fs/cgroup/worker/" + j.ID
+    os.MkdirAll(cgroupPath, 0755)
+    os.WriteFile(cgroupPath+"/memory.max", []byte(j.LimitBytes), 0644)
+
+    // 2. Prepare command with Namespace isolation (PID, NET, UTS)
+    j.Cmd = exec.Command(j.Command, j.Args...)
+    j.Cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{
+        Cloneflags: syscall.CLONE_NEWPID | syscall.CLONE_NEWNET | syscall.CLONE_NEWUTS,
+        Pdeathsig:  syscall.SIGKILL, // Kill job if worker server dies
+    }
+
+    // 3. Launch process and immediately attach to Cgroup
+    j.Cmd.Start()
+    // TODO: Note that there is a small race window where the process runs outside the cgroup. 
+    // A more robust solution would involve a fork/exec model where the child process adds itself to the cgroup before executing the target binary.
+    os.WriteFile(cgroupPath+"/cgroup.procs", []byte(strconv.itoa(j.Cmd.Process.Pid)), 0644)

+    return nil
+}
+```
+
+#### Output Streaming & Broadcasting 
+The `OutputBuffer` is implemented as a synchronized, in-memory store.
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***Replay***: Each `Job` maintains a maintains a byte slice of all historical output. New gRPC callers first read the existing buffer from their current offset.
+  *  ***Signaling***: We use `sync.Cond` for the broadcasting layer. When the library reads a chunk from the process pipes, it appends to the buffer and triggers `Broadcast()`, waking all dormant gRPC stream goroutines.
+
+##### Process Capture Stdout/Stderr to OutputBuffer Example
+```go
+func (b *OutputBuffer) Capture(source io.Reader) {
+    scanner := bufio.NewScanner(source)
+    for scanner.Scan() {
+        b.Lock()
+        // 1. Append to the "Replay" history
+        b.data = append(b.data, scanner.Bytes()...)
+        b.data = append(b.data, '\n')
+        b.Unlock()
+
+        // 2. "Broadcast" to all sleeping gRPC goroutines
+        b.L.Lock()
+        b.Broadcast()
+        b.L.Unlock()
+    }
+}
+```
+
+#### Security & Identity
+Security and Identity are paramount to protecting our servers from malicious actors. The following requirements ensure we protect the server:
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***mTLS 1.3***: Mandatory mutual TLS using a shared internal CA. We explicitly restrict the server to `TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384` to ensure modern cipher parity.
+  *  ***Identity-Based Auth***: The server extracts the `Subject.CommonName` (CN) from the client certificate. This CN is treated as the "OwnerID." Any request to `Stop`, `Status`, or `Stream` a job is rejected if the caller's CN does not match the job's `ExecutionSpecs.OwnerCommonName`.
+  *  ***Attack Surface Reduction***: The worker runs as a non-privileged user where possible, utilizing `CAP_SYS_ADMIN` only where required for Cgroup/Namespace setup.
+
+##### Verify Certificate Example
+```go
+func (s *workerServer) Authorize(ctx context.Context, jobID string) error {
+    // 1. Extract Peer info from gRPC context
+    p, _ := peer.FromContext(ctx)
+    tlsInfo := p.AuthInfo.(credentials.TLSInfo)
+    
+    // 2. Extract Common Name (CN) from the client certificate
+    clientCN := tlsInfo.State.PeerCertificates[0].Subject.CommonName
+    
+    // 3. Verify Ownership: Only the creator can manage the job
+    job := s.store.Get(jobID)
+    if job.OwnerCommonName != clientCN {
+        return status.Error(codes.PermissionDenied, "Identity mismatch")
+    }
+    
+    return nil
+}
+```
+
+#### Server Consideration
+Since the Server itself will be serving concurrent traffic with many clients, inflight goroutines should be sandboxed as well. We will need to consider graceful shutdowns and error handling to accommodate.
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***Graceful Shutdown***: If the server is shutdown or exits unexpectedly, we would like the server to gracefully shutdown. That means we'd like to handle each job and tell them to stop and let connected clients exit as well.
+  *  ***Error Handling***: Each `Job` will have a panic handler that will gracefully log errors to a channel before letting each process goroutine safely exit.
+
+
+##### Graceful Shutdown Example
+```go
+func (s *workerServer) GracefulShutdown(grpcServer *grpc.Server) {
+    // 1. Listen for OS termination signals (SIGINT, SIGTERM)
+    stop := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
+    signal.Notify(stop, os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
+    <-stop // Block until a signal is received
+
+    log.Println("Shutdown signal received. Cleaning up jobs...")
+
+    // 2. Stop the gRPC server from accepting new connections
+    grpcServer.GracefulStop()
+
+    // 3. Cleanup active jobs
+    s.mu.RLock()
+    defer s.mu.RUnlock()
+    for id, job := range s.jobs {
+        log.Printf("Terminating job %s...", id)
+        job.Stop() // This should trigger the SIGKILL to the process group
+    }
+
+    log.Println("Shutdown complete.")
+}
+```
+
+##### Panic Handler Example
+```go
+func (s *workerServer) HandlePanic(jobID string) {
+    if r := recover(); r != nil {
+        // 1. Log the error with stack trace for debugging
+        log.Printf("[PANIC] Job %s crashed: %v\nStack: %s", jobID, r, debug.Stack())
+
+        // 2. Mark the job state as failed so the client knows what happened
+        s.mu.Lock()
+        if job, ok := s.jobs[jobID]; ok {
+            job.State.Status = StatusFailed
+            job.State.EndTime = time.Now().UTC()
+        }
+        s.mu.Unlock()
+
+        // 3. (Optional) Send a specific error chunk to any active gRPC streamers
+    }
+}
+
+// Example usage in the orchestration:
+go func() {
+    defer s.HandlePanic(job.ID)
+    s.streamOutput(job)
+}()
+```
+
+### Library Structs
+The bulk of the data that will be kept in memory will be in the `Job` struct. Each job will have a status, as well as other pieces of metadata like ID, job commands and arguments.
+```go
+// Job is the container for each process initiated by a client.
+// It contains the metadata for the Command, Process, and Lifecycle. It also provides access to the Log Stream buffer.
+type Job struct {
+	sync.RWMutex
+
+	// ID is a unique UUID generated for the job, distinct from the OS PID. This is the same ID the client will be provided to manage processes
+	ID string
+	// Specs holds the command from the client
+	Specs ExecutionSpecs
+	// Proc holds live handles to the running process.
+	Proc ProcessHandle
+	// State tracks the current status and timing of the job.
+	State Lifecycle
+	// Limit defines the resource boundaries for the process on the linux system.
+	Limit ResourceLimits
+	// Stream manages the in-memory buffer for replayable output.
+	Stream *OutputBuffer
+}
+
+// OutputBuffer implements a thread-safe, multi-consumer broadcaster for process output
+type OutputBuffer struct {
+	sync.RWMutex
+	// cond is a condition variable used to wake up dormant client streamers when new data arrives.
+	sync.Cond
+
+	// data is the in-memory store of all stdout/stderr produced by the process.
+	data []byte
+	// closed indicates the process has finished writing to the buffer.
+	closed bool
+
+}
+```
+
+#### Subtypes
+```go
+// JobStatus represents the current lifecycle state of a worker job.
+type JobStatus string
+
+const (
+	// StatusRunning indicates the process has started and is currently active.
+	StatusRunning JobStatus = "running"
+	// StatusStopped indicates the process was manually terminated by a user request.
+	StatusStopped JobStatus = "stopped"
+	// StatusCompleted indicates the process exited on its own with a zero exit code.
+	StatusCompleted JobStatus = "completed"
+	// StatusFailed indicates the process exited with a non-zero exit code or system error.
+	StatusFailed JobStatus = "failed"
+)
+
+// ExecutionSpecs defines the parameters provided by the client when a job is first created.
+type ExecutionSpecs struct {
+	// Command is the path to the executable to be run.
+	Command string
+	// Args is the list of arguments passed to the Command.
+	Args []string
+	// OwnerCommonName is the Common Name extracted from the client's TLS certificate, used for ownership-based authorization.
+	OwnerCommonName string
+}
+
+// ResourceLimits defines the kernel-level constraints applied to a job.
+// These are implemented via Cgroups on Linux.
+type ResourceLimits struct {
+	// MemoryLimitBytes is the maximum physical memory the process tree can consume.
+	MemoryLimitBytes int64
+	// CPULimitPercent is the maximum CPU usage allowed (e.g., 0.5 for 50% of a core).
+	CPULimitPercent float64
+}
+
+// ProcessHandle maintains the live OS-level handles and controls for the process.
+type ProcessHandle struct {
+	// PID is the Operating System's Process ID.
+	PID int
+	// cmd is the underlying Go exec.Cmd instance managing the lifecycle.
+	cmd *exec.Cmd
+	// cancel is the context cancellation function used to signal a stop.
+	cancel context.CancelFunc
+}
+
+// Lifecycle tracks the temporal state and exit results of a job.
+type Lifecycle struct {
+	// Status is the current machine-state of the job.
+	Status JobStatus
+	// ExitCode is the exit code returned by the process upon termination.
+	ExitCode int
+	// StartTime is the UTC timestamp when the process was successfully started.
+	StartTime time.Time
+	// EndTime is the UTC timestamp when the process was ended.
+	EndTime time.Time
+}
+```
+
+
+
+### Client <> Server gRPC Specification
+The client to server schema will be using protobuf to support a standard gRPC API. The Start/Stop/Status apis will support synchronous job management, while Stream will return a stream of logs until the client wants to stop listening.
+
+#### Service Definition
+```protobuf
+service JobWorker {
+  rpc Start(StartRequest) returns (StartResponse);
+  rpc Stop(StopRequest) returns (StopResponse);
+  rpc Status(StatusRequest) returns (StatusResponse);
+  // Returns a stream that replays history and broadcasts new updates
+  rpc Stream(StreamRequest) returns (stream LogChunk);
+}
+```
+
+#### Start Job
+```protobuf
+message ResourceLimits {
+  uint64 memory_bytes = 1;
+  float cpu_max_percent = 2; // e.g., 50.0 for 50% of CPU time.
+}
+
+message StartRequest {
+  string command = 1;
+  repeated string args = 2;
+  ResourceLimits limits = 3;
+}
+
+message StartResponse {
+  string job_id = 1;
+}
+```
+
+#### Stop Job
+```protobuf
+message StopRequest {
+  string job_id = 1;
+}
+
+message StopResponse {}
+```
+
+#### Get Status
+```protobuf
+message StatusRequest {
+  string job_id = 1;
+}
+
+message StatusResponse {
+  string job_id = 1;
+  string state = 2;
+  int32 exit_code = 3;
+  // Added to match UX requirements
+  string command = 4;
+  repeated string args = 5;
+  google.protobuf.Timestamp started_at = 6;
+  google.protobuf.Timestamp ended_at = 7;
+}
+```
+
+#### Stream Job
+```protobuf
+message StreamRequest {
+  string job_id = 1;
+}
+
+message LogChunk {
+  bytes data = 1;
+  // Distinguishes between output streams
+  enum Source {
+    STDOUT = 0;
+    STDERR = 1;
+  }
+  Source source = 2;
+  google.protobuf.Timestamp timestamp = 3;

Agreed, let me flesh that out instead of hand-waving it. 

There are three main cases. 
1. The command ends on it's own
2. The user calls Stop()
3. The command is indefinite

If the command finishes on it's own it will automatically cleanup the process resources, and if the user calls `Stop()` the same will happen. 

In the last case where a command runs indefinitely and the user doesn't do cleanup, I think I would need to know more about the user behavior.
Does a User expect to let commands run indefinitely like my UX job example `while true; echo hello`? Should we require a TTL? Or should there be a default TTL? Can those TTLs be indefinite too? E.G a repeat scheduled task?

The mention of Attack Surface Reduction was intended as a design principle for prod. In that scenario, we wouldn't 'regain' privileges; instead, the server would start with elevated privileges, perform the sensitive Namespace/Cgroup setup for the child, and then the Shim process would explicitly drop all inherited privileges (using setuid/setgid and clearing the capability bounding set) immediately before the syscall.Execve() call. This ensures the user's arbitrary payload never runs with the server's elevated permissions.

+### Architecture and Subsystems
+The system consists of three main components:
+1.  **Worker Library**: A low-level wrapper around `os/exec` and `syscall`. It manages the process lifecycle, namespace isolation, and Cgroup attachment.
+      * Remote Process Execution: [os/exec](https://pkg.go.dev/os/exec)
+      * Resource Isolation: [sys/unix](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/sys/unix)

+          end

+          subgraph "Job 2 Sandbox"
+              P2((Process 2))
+          end
+
+          CG[[Cgroups v2]]
+          NS[[Namespaces]]
+      end
+    end
+
+    %% Flow
+    C1 -- "Job 1 (Stream)" --> SVR
+    C2 -- "Job 2 (Start)" --> SVR
+    SVR <--> MAP
+
+    MAP --> B1
+    MAP --> B2
+    
+    SVR --> P1
+    SVR --> P2
+
+    P1 -.-> B1 -.-> SVR
+    P2 -.-> B2 -.-> SVR
+
+    P1 & P2 --- CG
+    P1 & P2 --- NS
+```
+

+```mermaid
+sequenceDiagram
+    autonumber
+    participant C as CLI
+    participant S as gRPC Server
+    participant L as Library
+    participant K as Linux Kernel
+
+    Note over C, K: StartRequest() Sequence
+    C->>S: StartRequest()
+    S->>S: Authenticate()
+    S->>L: InitJob(Specs, Limits)
+    L->>K: mkdir /sys/fs/cgroup/job-123

+    L->>K: fork() with CLONE_NEW*

+    L->>K: write PID to cgroup.procs

+    L->>C: Replay historical bytes

+      * Resource Isolation: [sys/unix](https://pkg.go.dev/golang.org/x/sys/unix)

+    C2 -- "Job 2 (Start)" --> SVR

+    MAP --> B2
+    
+    SVR --> P1
+    SVR --> P2

+    P2 -.-> B2 -.-> SVR

+### Implementation
+#### Process Orchestration
+We will utilize `os/exec.Cmd` while overriding `SysProcAttr` to handle kernel-level isolation.
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***Isolation***: Processes are spawned into new namespaces (PID, UTS, Network) using `CLONE_NEW*` flags to prevent host-level lateral movement.

+  *  ***Resource Constraints***: We will leverage Cgroups v2. Upon job initiation, the library creates a unique Cgroup leaf node at `/sys/fs/cgroup/worker/<job_id>/`. +  *  ***Process Tree Termination***: To prevent orphaned processes, the library will set the process group ID `Setpgid: true`. That means that on `Stop()`, a `SIGKILL` is sent to the negative PID (e.g., -1234) to terminate the entire process group.

+    os.MkdirAll(cgroupPath, 0755)
+    os.WriteFile(cgroupPath+"/memory.max", []byte(j.LimitBytes), 0644)

+    // 2. Prepare command with Namespace isolation (PID, NET, UTS)
+    j.Cmd = exec.Command(j.Command, j.Args...)
+    j.Cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{
+        Cloneflags: syscall.CLONE_NEWPID | syscall.CLONE_NEWNET | syscall.CLONE_NEWUTS,
+        Pdeathsig:  syscall.SIGKILL, // Kill job if worker server dies
+    }
+
+    // 3. Launch process and immediately attach to Cgroup
+    j.Cmd.Start()

+    os.WriteFile(cgroupPath+"/cgroup.procs", []byte(strconv.itoa(j.Cmd.Process.Pid)), 0644)
+
+    return nil
+}
+```

+#### Output Streaming & Broadcasting 
+The `OutputBuffer` is implemented as a synchronized, in-memory store.
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***Replay***: Each `Job` maintains a maintains a byte slice of all historical output. New gRPC callers first read the existing buffer from their current offset.
+  *  ***Signaling***: We use `sync.Cond` for the broadcasting layer. In the case a reader is blocked due to a disconnected client, we will need to watch the gRPC ctx on a separate channel. If ctx is cancelled, we will need to wake up all readers using Broadcast() and ensure each reader is always watching the ctx before reading data.

+```go
+func (b *OutputBuffer) Capture(source io.Reader) {
+    scanner := bufio.NewScanner(source)
+    for scanner.Scan() {
+        b.Lock()
+        // 1. Append to the "Replay" history
+        b.data = append(b.data, scanner.Bytes()...)
+        b.data = append(b.data, '\n')
+        b.Unlock()
+
+        // 2. "Broadcast" to all sleeping gRPC goroutines
+        b.L.Lock()
+        b.Broadcast()
+        b.L.Unlock()
+    }
+}
+```

+Security and Identity are paramount to protecting our servers from malicious actors. The following requirements ensure we protect the server:

+  *  ***mTLS 1.3***: Mandatory mutual TLS using a shared internal CA. We explicitly restrict the server to `TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384` to ensure modern cipher parity.

+    // 2. Extract Common Name (CN) from the client certificate

+

+    }
+    
+    return nil
+}
+```

+    }

+    log.Println("Shutdown complete.")

+func (s *workerServer) HandlePanic(jobID string) {
+    if r := recover(); r != nil {

+        }
+        s.mu.Unlock()

+    }

+    participant S as gRPC Server
+    participant L as Library

+    S->>L: InitJob(Specs, Limits)

+#### Process Orchestration
+We will utilize `os/exec.Cmd` while overriding `SysProcAttr` to handle kernel-level isolation.

+  *  ***Isolation***: Processes are spawned into new namespaces (PID, UTS, Network) using `CLONE_NEW*` flags to prevent host-level lateral movement. 
+        * *NOTE: Creating a new Network namespace will disallow networking calls. Future work might include adding back networking capabilities while taking advantage of the current sandboxing of each process.*
+  *  ***Resource Constraints***: We will leverage Cgroups v2. Upon job initiation, the library creates a unique Cgroup leaf node at `/sys/fs/cgroup/worker/<job_id>/`. +    j.Cmd = exec.Command(j.Command, j.Args...)
+    j.Cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{

+The `OutputBuffer` is implemented as a synchronized, in-memory store.

+  *  ***Replay***: Each `Job` maintains a maintains a byte slice of all historical output. New gRPC callers first read the existing buffer from their current offset.

If ctx is cancelled, we will need to wake up all readers using Broadcast() and ensure each reader is always watching the ctx before reading data.

+```go
+func (b *OutputBuffer) Capture(source io.Reader) {
+    scanner := bufio.NewScanner(source)
+    for scanner.Scan() {
+        b.Lock()
+        // 1. Append to the "Replay" history
+        b.data = append(b.data, scanner.Bytes()...)
+        b.data = append(b.data, '\n')
+        b.Unlock()
+
+        // 2. "Broadcast" to all sleeping gRPC goroutines
+        b.L.Lock()
+        b.Broadcast()
+        b.L.Unlock()
+    }

+```

+Security and Identity are paramount to protecting our servers from malicious actors. The following requirements ensure we protect the server:
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***mTLS 1.3***: Mandatory mutual TLS using a shared internal CA. We explicitly restrict the server to `TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384` to ensure modern cipher parity.
+  *  ***Identity-Based Auth***: The server extracts the `Subject.CommonName` (CN) from the client certificate. This CN is treated as the "OwnerID." Any request to `Stop`, `Status`, or `Stream` a job is rejected if the caller's CN does not match the job's `ExecutionSpecs.OwnerCommonName`.

+```go

+    // 1. Extract Peer info from gRPC context

+    tlsInfo := p.AuthInfo.(credentials.TLSInfo)
+    
+    // 2. Extract Common Name (CN) from the client certificate
+    clientCN := tlsInfo.State.PeerCertificates[0].Subject.CommonName
+    
+    // 3. Verify Ownership: Only the creator can manage the job
+    job := s.store.Get(jobID)
+    if job.OwnerCommonName != clientCN {

+    }

+    return nil
+}
+```
+

+Since the Server itself will be serving concurrent traffic with many clients, inflight goroutines should be sandboxed as well. We will need to consider graceful shutdowns and error handling to accommodate.
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***Graceful Shutdown***: If the server is shutdown or exits unexpectedly, we would like the server to gracefully shutdown. That means we'd like to handle each job and tell them to stop and let connected clients exit as well.

+    }

+        log.Printf("[PANIC] Job %s crashed: %v\nStack: %s", jobID, r, debug.Stack())

+### Implementation
+#### Process Orchestration
+We utilize `os/exec.Cmd` to execute processes directly on the host. To ensure a zero-race environment, the library employs a `Self-Jailing Shim` pattern, where the child process joins the Cgroup prior to executing the target binary.
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***Resource Constraints***: We will leverage Cgroups v2. Upon job initiation, the library creates a unique Cgroup leaf node at `/sys/fs/cgroup/worker/<job_id>/`. Limits are written to `memory.max`, `cpu.max`, `io.max` before the process is migrated into the group to ensure each process is resource constrained before fork() is called.
+      * Process Memory & CPU: Limits are written to `memory.max` and `cpu.max` before the process starts.
+      * Disk I/O: Throughput and IOPS are throttled via `io.max`. This file accepts structured strings in the format `$MAJ:$MIN rbps=$N wbps=$N`, allowing the library to cap the bytes-per-second and operations-per-second for specific block devices.
+  *  ***Process Tree Termination***: To prevent orphaned processes and avoid the PID-reuse races inherent in signaling process groups, the library will leverage `cgroup.kill` to terminate the entire process group```

+##### Start Process Example
+**NOTE** *Implementation Clarity: For the sake of readability, the following Go code examples omit exhaustive error handling, and certain edge-case validations. A production implementation would include comprehensive error wrapping and defensive checks for all syscalls and filesystem operations.*

+func (j *Job) Start() error {
+    // Setup the Cgroup jail
+    j.initCgroup();
+
+    // Prepare the execution command
+    j.Proc.cmd = exec.Command(j.Specs.Command, j.Specs.Arguments...)
+    j.Proc.cmd.Stdout = j.OutputBuffer
+    j.Proc.cmd.cmd.Stderr = j.OutputBuffer

+    j.Proc.cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{
+        Ptrace:    true,            // By starting the process with Ptrace, the parent can intercept it before execution, attach it to the cgroup, and then detach to resume execution, eliminating any race condition where the process runs without limits.
+        Pdeathsig: syscall.SIGKILL, // Kills child if server crashes
+    }
+
+    // Launch and Jail
+    j.Proc.cmd.Start()
+    pid := j.Proc.cmd.Process.Pid
+    if err := j.attachToCgroup(pid); err != nil {
+        j.Proc.cmd.Process.Kill()
+        return err
+    }
+
+    // Handle Zombie Processes
+    go j.reap()
+
+    // Update Job Status
+    j.UpdateStatus(StatusRunning)
+    return nil
+}
+
+```

+// and detaches ptrace to resume execution in the constrained environment.

+// recording, and Cgroup directory removal.

+func (j *Job) Stop() error {

+    if j.State.Status != StatusRunning {
+        return nil

+    // Writing "1" to cgroup.kill kills every process in the cgroup immediately.
+    cgroupKillPath := filepath.Join("/sys/fs/cgroup/worker", j.ID, "cgroup.kill")
+    err := os.WriteFile(cgroupKillPath, []byte("1"), 0644)
+    if err != nil {

+        if j.Proc.cmd.Process != nil {

+    }

+#### Output Streaming & Broadcasting 
+The `OutputBuffer` is implemented as a synchronized, in-memory store.
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***Replay***: Each `Job` maintains a maintains a byte slice of all historical output. New gRPC callers first read the existing buffer from their current offset.
+  *  ***Signaling***: We use `sync.Cond` for the broadcasting layer. When the library reads a chunk from the process pipes, it appends to the buffer and triggers `Broadcast()`, waking all dormant gRPC stream goroutines. In the case a reader is blocked due to a disconnected client, we will need to watch the gRPC ctx on a separate channel. If ctx is cancelled, we will need to wake up all readers using Broadcast() and ensure each reader is always watching the ctx before reading data.
+

+```go
+// Write implements the io.Writer interface. This allows the OutputBuffer
+// to be assigned directly to exec.Cmd.Stdout and Stderr.
+func (b *OutputBuffer) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	// We must copy the slice because the caller (os/exec) may reuse the backing array.
+	data := make([]byte, len(p))
+	copy(data, p)
+
+	entry := LogEntry{
+		Data:      data,
+		Timestamp: time.Now().UTC(),
+    // TODO: Create wrapper for OutputBuffer that assigns the correct Source

+	defer b.Unlock()
+
+	b.entries = append(b.entries, entry)

+```

+##### Stream Example
+```go
+// Stream captures the logic for a gRPC server sending logs to a client.
+func (s *workerServer) Stream(req *StreamRequest, stream JobWorker_StreamServer) error {
+	job := s.store.Get(req.JobId)
+	var offset int
+
+	for {
+		job.Stream.RLock()
+		// Wait until there is new data or the job is finished
+		for offset >= len(job.Stream.entries) && !job.Stream.closed {
+			job.Stream.cond.Wait() 
+		}
+
+		// Check if we have new entries to send
+		var entries []LogEntry
+		if offset < len(job.Stream.entries) {
+			entries = job.Stream.entries[offset:]
+			offset = len(job.Stream.entries)
+		}
+		
+		isClosed := job.Stream.closed
+		job.Stream.RUnlock()
+
+		// Send entries over gRPC
+		for _, entry := range entries {
+			if err := stream.Send(mapToProto(entry)); err != nil {
+				return err
+			}
+		}
+
+		if isClosed {
+			return nil
+		}
+	}
+}
+```
+
+#### Security & Identity
+Security and Identity are paramount to protecting our servers from malicious actors. The following requirements ensure we protect the server:
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***mTLS 1.3***: Mandatory mutual TLS using a shared internal CA. We explicitly restrict the server to `TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384` to ensure modern cipher parity.
+  *  ***Identity-Based Auth***: The server extracts the `Subject.CommonName` (CN) from the client certificate. This CN is treated as the "Owner." Any request to `Stop`, `Status`, or `Stream` a job is rejected if the caller's CN does not match the job's `ExecutionSpecs.OwnerCommonName`.
+
+##### Verify Certificate Example
+```go
+func (s *workerServer) Authorize(ctx context.Context, jobID string) error {
+    // Extract Peer info from gRPC context
+    p, _ := peer.FromContext(ctx)
+    tlsInfo := p.AuthInfo.(credentials.TLSInfo)
+    
+    // Extract Common Name (CN) from the client certificate
+    clientCN := tlsInfo.State.PeerCertificates[0].Subject.CommonName
+    
+    // Verify Ownership: Only the creator can manage the job
+    job := s.store.Get(jobID)
+    if job.OwnerCommonName != clientCN {
+        return status.Error(codes.PermissionDenied, "Identity mismatch")
+    }
+    
+    return nil
+}
+```
+
+#### Server Consideration
+Since the Server itself will be serving concurrent traffic with many clients, inflight goroutines should be sandboxed as well. We will need to consider error handling to accommodate.
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***Error Handling***: Each `Job` will have a panic handler that will gracefully log errors to a channel before letting each process goroutine safely exit.
+
+##### Panic Handler Example
+```go
+// HandlePanic ensures that a failure in a management goroutine (like log capture)
+// does not terminate the underlying OS process or incorrectly modify the job's state.
+func (s *workerServer) HandlePanic(jobID string) {
+    if r := recover(); r != nil {
+        // Log the critical management failure with a full stack trace.
+        // We do not call job.Stop() or modify job.State here, as the 
+        // underlying process is still healthy in its Cgroup.
+        log.Printf("[CRITICAL] Management goroutine panic for Job %s: %v\nStack: %s", jobID, r, debug.Stack())
+    }
+}
+
+// Example usage in the orchestration:
+go func() {
+    defer s.HandlePanic(job.ID)
+    s.streamOutput(job)
+}()
+```
+
+### Library Structs
+The bulk of the data that will be kept in memory will be in the `Job` struct. Each job will have a status, as well as other pieces of metadata like ID, job commands and arguments.
+```go
+// Job is the container for each process initiated by a client.
+// It contains the metadata for the Command, Process, and Lifecycle. It also provides access to the Log Stream buffer.
+type Job struct {
+	sync.RWMutex
+
+	// ID is a unique UUID generated for the job, distinct from the OS PID. This is the same ID the client will be provided to manage processes
+	ID string
+	// Specs holds the command from the client
+	Specs ExecutionSpecs
+	// Proc holds live handles to the running process.
+	Proc ProcessHandle
+	// State tracks the current status and timing of the job.
+	State Lifecycle
+	// Limit defines the resource boundaries for the process on the linux system.
+	Limit ResourceLimits
+	// Stream manages the in-memory buffer for replayable output.
+	Stream *OutputBuffer
+}
+
+// OutputSource is the source type of each log entry
+type OutputSource int32
+
+const (
+  // OutputSourceUnspecified indicates the source is unspecified
+  OutputSourceUnspecified OutputSource = 0
+  // OutputSourceStdout is Standard Output from the process.
+	OutputSourceStdout      OutputSource = 1
+  // OutputSourceStderr is Standard Error from the process.
+	OutputSourceStderr      OutputSource = 2
+)
+
+// LogEntry preserves the metadata for a specific chunk of output.
+type LogEntry struct {
+  // Data contains an unstructured byte array for the current entry from the process
+	Data      []byte
+  // Source is the type of output log from the process
+	Source    OutputSource
+  // Timestamp is the timestamp of the Capture event for this log
+	Timestamp time.Time
+}
+
+// OutputBuffer implements a thread-safe, multi-consumer broadcaster for process output
+type OutputBuffer struct {
+	sync.RWMutex
+	// cond is a condition variable used to wake up dormant client streamers when new data arrives.
+	cond *sync.Cond
+	// entries is the in-memory store of all stdout/stderr produced by the process.
+  entries []LogEntry
+	// closed indicates the process has finished writing to the buffer.
+	closed bool
+}
+```
+
+#### Subtypes
+```go
+// JobStatus represents the current lifecycle state of a worker job.
+type JobStatus int32
+
+const (
+  // StatusUnspecified indicates the status is unspecified
+  StatusUnspecified JobStatus = 0
+  // StatusRunning indicates the process has started and is currently active.
+	StatusRunning     JobStatus = 1
+  // StatusStopped indicates the process was manually terminated by a user request.
+	StatusStopped     JobStatus = 2
+  // StatusCompleted indicates the process exited on its own with a zero exit code.
+	StatusCompleted   JobStatus = 3
+  // StatusFailed indicates the process exited with a non-zero exit code or system error.
+	StatusFailed      JobStatus = 4
+)
+
+// ExecutionSpecs defines the parameters provided by the client when a job is first created.
+type ExecutionSpecs struct {
+	// Command is the path to the executable to be run.
+	Command string
+  // Arguments is the path to the executable to be run.
+	Arguments []string
+	// OwnerCommonName is the Common Name extracted from the client's TLS certificate, used for ownership-based authorization.
+	OwnerCommonName string
+}
+
+// ResourceLimits defines the kernel-level constraints applied to a job.
+// These are implemented via Cgroups on Linux.
+type ResourceLimits struct {
+	// MemoryLimitBytes is the maximum physical memory the process tree can consume.
+	MemoryLimitBytes int64
+	// CPULimitPercent is the maximum CPU usage allowed (e.g., 0.5 for 50% of a core).
+	CPULimitPercent float64
+  // IOLimit is the maximum IO Read and Write for the process. It Requires specific properties to generate a string necessary for linux CGroup limits
+	IOLimit LinuxIOLimit
+}
+
+// IOLimit is the spec needed to generate a structured string for the linux cgroup
+type LinuxIOLimit struct {
+    Major      int
+    Minor      int

+3.  **CLI**: A Cobra-based implementation that manages the mTLS handshake and renders gRPC stream chunks to the local TTY.

+### Implementation
+#### Process Orchestration
+We utilize `os/exec.Cmd` to execute processes directly on the host. To ensure a zero-race environment, the library employs a `Self-Jailing Shim` pattern, where the child process joins the Cgroup prior to executing the target binary.
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***Resource Constraints***: We will leverage Cgroups v2. Upon job initiation, the library creates a unique Cgroup leaf node at `/sys/fs/cgroup/worker/<job_id>/`. Limits are written to `memory.max`, `cpu.max`, `io.max` before the process is migrated into the group to ensure each process is resource constrained before fork() is called.
+      * Process Memory & CPU: Limits are written to `memory.max` and `cpu.max` before the process starts.
+      * Disk I/O: Throughput and IOPS are throttled via `io.max`. This file accepts structured strings in the format `$MAJ:$MIN rbps=$N wbps=$N`, allowing the library to cap the bytes-per-second and operations-per-second for specific block devices.
+  *  ***Process Tree Termination***: To prevent orphaned processes and avoid the PID-reuse races inherent in signaling process groups, the library will leverage `cgroup.kill` to terminate the entire process group```
+
+##### Start Process Example
+**NOTE** *Implementation Clarity: For the sake of readability, the following Go code examples omit exhaustive error handling, and certain edge-case validations. A production implementation would include comprehensive error wrapping and defensive checks for all syscalls and filesystem operations.*
+
+```go
+func (j *Job) Start() error {
+    // Setup the Cgroup jail
+    j.initCgroup();
+
+    // Prepare the execution command
+    j.Proc.cmd = exec.Command(j.Specs.Command, j.Specs.Arguments...)
+    j.Proc.cmd.Stdout = j.OutputBuffer
+    j.Proc.cmd.cmd.Stderr = j.OutputBuffer
+
+    j.Proc.cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{
+        Ptrace:    true,            // By starting the process with Ptrace, the parent can intercept it before execution, attach it to the cgroup, and then detach to resume execution, eliminating any race condition where the process runs without limits.
+        Pdeathsig: syscall.SIGKILL, // Kills child if server crashes
+    }
+
+    // Launch and Jail
+    j.Proc.cmd.Start()
+    pid := j.Proc.cmd.Process.Pid
+    if err := j.attachToCgroup(pid); err != nil {
+        j.Proc.cmd.Process.Kill()
+        return err
+    }
+
+    // Handle Zombie Processes
+    go j.reap()
+
+    // Update Job Status
+    j.UpdateStatus(StatusRunning)
+    return nil
+}
+
+```

+// and detaches ptrace to resume execution in the constrained environment.
+func (j *Job) attachToCgroup(pid int) error { ... }
+
+// reap blocks on the process exit and handles resource cleanup, exit code
+// recording, and Cgroup directory removal.
+func (j *Job) reap() { ... }

+##### Stop Process Example
+```go
+func (j *Job) Stop() error {
+    j.Lock()
+    defer j.Unlock()
+
+    // Check if the job is already finished to avoid unnecessary syscalls
+    if j.State.Status != StatusRunning {
+        return nil
+    }
+
+    // Atomic Termination via Cgroup v2
+    // Writing "1" to cgroup.kill kills every process in the cgroup immediately.
+    cgroupKillPath := filepath.Join("/sys/fs/cgroup/worker", j.ID, "cgroup.kill")
+    err := os.WriteFile(cgroupKillPath, []byte("1"), 0644)
+    if err != nil {
+        // Fallback: If cgroup.kill fails (e.g., older kernel), use traditional SIGKILL
+        if j.Proc.cmd.Process != nil {
+            return j.Proc.cmd.Process.Kill()
+        }
+        return fmt.Errorf("failed to terminate cgroup: %w", err)
+    }
+
+    // Update Lifecycle State
+    j.UpdateStatus(StatusStopped)
+    return nil
+}
+```
+#### Output Streaming & Broadcasting 
+The `OutputBuffer` is implemented as a synchronized, in-memory store.
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***Replay***: Each `Job` maintains a maintains a byte slice of all historical output. New gRPC callers first read the existing buffer from their current offset.
+  *  ***Signaling***: We use `sync.Cond` for the broadcasting layer. When the library reads a chunk from the process pipes, it appends to the buffer and triggers `Broadcast()`, waking all dormant gRPC stream goroutines. In the case a reader is blocked due to a disconnected client, we will need to watch the gRPC ctx on a separate channel. If ctx is cancelled, we will need to wake up all readers using Broadcast() and ensure each reader is always watching the ctx before reading data.
+
+##### Implement io.Writer for OutputBuffer Example
+```go
+// Write implements the io.Writer interface. This allows the OutputBuffer
+// to be assigned directly to exec.Cmd.Stdout and Stderr.
+func (b *OutputBuffer) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
+	// We must copy the slice because the caller (os/exec) may reuse the backing array.
+	data := make([]byte, len(p))
+	copy(data, p)
+
+	entry := LogEntry{
+		Data:      data,
+		Timestamp: time.Now().UTC(),
+    // TODO: Create wrapper for OutputBuffer that assigns the correct Source
+		Source: OutputSourceStdout,
+	}
+
+	b.Lock()
+	defer b.Unlock()
+
+	b.entries = append(b.entries, entry)
+	b.cond.Broadcast()
+
+	return len(p), nil
+}
+```
+
+##### Stream Example
+```go
+// Stream captures the logic for a gRPC server sending logs to a client.
+func (s *workerServer) Stream(req *StreamRequest, stream JobWorker_StreamServer) error {
+	job := s.store.Get(req.JobId)
+	var offset int
+
+	for {
+		job.Stream.RLock()
+		// Wait until there is new data or the job is finished
+		for offset >= len(job.Stream.entries) && !job.Stream.closed {
+			job.Stream.cond.Wait() 
+		}
+
+		// Check if we have new entries to send
+		var entries []LogEntry
+		if offset < len(job.Stream.entries) {
+			entries = job.Stream.entries[offset:]
+			offset = len(job.Stream.entries)
+		}
+		
+		isClosed := job.Stream.closed
+		job.Stream.RUnlock()
+
+		// Send entries over gRPC
+		for _, entry := range entries {
+			if err := stream.Send(mapToProto(entry)); err != nil {
+				return err
+			}
+		}
+
+		if isClosed {
+			return nil
+		}
+	}
+}
+```
+
+#### Security & Identity
+Security and Identity are paramount to protecting our servers from malicious actors. The following requirements ensure we protect the server:
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***mTLS 1.3***: Mandatory mutual TLS using a shared internal CA. We explicitly restrict the server to `TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384` to ensure modern cipher parity.
+  *  ***Identity-Based Auth***: The server extracts the `Subject.CommonName` (CN) from the client certificate. This CN is treated as the "Owner." Any request to `Stop`, `Status`, or `Stream` a job is rejected if the caller's CN does not match the job's `ExecutionSpecs.OwnerCommonName`.
+
+##### Verify Certificate Example
+```go
+func (s *workerServer) Authorize(ctx context.Context, jobID string) error {
+    // Extract Peer info from gRPC context
+    p, _ := peer.FromContext(ctx)
+    tlsInfo := p.AuthInfo.(credentials.TLSInfo)
+    
+    // Extract Common Name (CN) from the client certificate
+    clientCN := tlsInfo.State.PeerCertificates[0].Subject.CommonName
+    
+    // Verify Ownership: Only the creator can manage the job
+    job := s.store.Get(jobID)
+    if job.OwnerCommonName != clientCN {
+        return status.Error(codes.PermissionDenied, "Identity mismatch")
+    }
+    
+    return nil
+}
+```
+
+#### Server Consideration
+Since the Server itself will be serving concurrent traffic with many clients, inflight goroutines should be sandboxed as well. We will need to consider error handling to accommodate.
+* Technical Requirements:
+  *  ***Error Handling***: Each `Job` will have a panic handler that will gracefully log errors to a channel before letting each process goroutine safely exit.
+
+##### Panic Handler Example
+```go
+// HandlePanic ensures that a failure in a management goroutine (like log capture)
+// does not terminate the underlying OS process or incorrectly modify the job's state.
+func (s *workerServer) HandlePanic(jobID string) {
+    if r := recover(); r != nil {
+        // Log the critical management failure with a full stack trace.
+        // We do not call job.Stop() or modify job.State here, as the 
+        // underlying process is still healthy in its Cgroup.
+        log.Printf("[CRITICAL] Management goroutine panic for Job %s: %v\nStack: %s", jobID, r, debug.Stack())
+    }
+}
+
+// Example usage in the orchestration:
+go func() {
+    defer s.HandlePanic(job.ID)
+    s.streamOutput(job)
+}()
+```
+
+### Library Structs
+The bulk of the data that will be kept in memory will be in the `Job` struct. Each job will have a status, as well as other pieces of metadata like ID, job commands and arguments.
+```go
+// Job is the container for each process initiated by a client.
+// It contains the metadata for the Command, Process, and Lifecycle. It also provides access to the Log Stream buffer.
+type Job struct {
+	sync.RWMutex
+
+	// ID is a unique UUID generated for the job, distinct from the OS PID. This is the same ID the client will be provided to manage processes
+	ID string
+	// Specs holds the command from the client
+	Specs ExecutionSpecs
+	// Proc holds live handles to the running process.
+	Proc ProcessHandle
+	// State tracks the current status and timing of the job.
+	State Lifecycle
+	// Limit defines the resource boundaries for the process on the linux system.
+	Limit ResourceLimits
+	// Stream manages the in-memory buffer for replayable output.
+	Stream *OutputBuffer
+}
+
+// OutputSource is the source type of each log entry
+type OutputSource int32
+
+const (
+  // OutputSourceUnspecified indicates the source is unspecified
+  OutputSourceUnspecified OutputSource = 0
+  // OutputSourceStdout is Standard Output from the process.
+	OutputSourceStdout      OutputSource = 1
+  // OutputSourceStderr is Standard Error from the process.
+	OutputSourceStderr      OutputSource = 2
+)
+
+// LogEntry preserves the metadata for a specific chunk of output.
+type LogEntry struct {
+  // Data contains an unstructured byte array for the current entry from the process
+	Data      []byte
+  // Source is the type of output log from the process

+  // Timestamp is the timestamp of the Capture event for this log
+	Timestamp time.Time
+}
+
+// OutputBuffer implements a thread-safe, multi-consumer broadcaster for process output
+type OutputBuffer struct {
+	sync.RWMutex
+	// cond is a condition variable used to wake up dormant client streamers when new data arrives.
+	cond *sync.Cond
+	// entries is the in-memory store of all stdout/stderr produced by the process.
+  entries []LogEntry
+	// closed indicates the process has finished writing to the buffer.
+	closed bool
+}
+```

+// Stream captures the logic for a gRPC server sending logs to a client.
+func (s *workerServer) Stream(req *StreamRequest, stream JobWorker_StreamServer) error {
+    job := s.store.Get(req.JobId)
+    var offset int
+    ctx := stream.Context()
+
+    // This goroutine ensures that if a client disconnects, we broadcast to all
+    // waiting streamers for this job, preventing a goroutine leak.
+    go func() {
+        <-ctx.Done()
+        job.Stream.cond.Broadcast()
+    }()
+
+    for {
+        // Before locking, check if the client has already disconnected.
+        if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
+            return err
+        }
+
+        job.Stream.RLock()
+        // Wait until there is new data, the job is finished, or the client has disconnected.
+        for offset >= len(job.Stream.entries) && !job.Stream.closed && ctx.Err() == nil {
+            job.Stream.cond.Wait()
+        }
+
+        var entriesToSend []LogEntry
+        if offset < len(job.Stream.entries) {
+            entriesToSend = job.Stream.entries[offset:]
+            offset = len(job.Stream.entries)

+// It contains the metadata for the Command, Process, and Lifecycle. It also provides access to the Log Stream buffer.
+type Job struct {

+	// Specs holds the command from the client

+// Job is the container for each process initiated by a client.
+// It contains the metadata for the Command, Process, and Lifecycle. It also provides access to the Log Stream buffer.
+type Job struct {
+	sync.RWMutex
+
+	// ID is a unique UUID generated for the job, distinct from the OS PID. This is the same ID the client will be provided to manage processes
+	ID string
+	// Specs holds the command from the client
+	Specs ExecutionSpecs
+	// Proc holds live handles to the running process.
+	Proc ProcessHandle
+	// State tracks the current status and timing of the job.
+	State Lifecycle
+	// Limit defines the resource boundaries for the process on the linux system.
+	Limit ResourceLimits
+	// Stream manages the in-memory buffer for replayable output.
+	Stream *OutputBuffer
+}
+
+// OutputSource is the source type of each log entry
+type OutputSource int32
+
+const (
+  // OutputSourceUnspecified indicates the source is unspecified
+  OutputSourceUnspecified OutputSource = 0
+  // OutputSourceStdout is Standard Output from the process.
+	OutputSourceStdout      OutputSource = 1
+  // OutputSourceStderr is Standard Error from the process.
+	OutputSourceStderr      OutputSource = 2
+)
+
+// LogEntry preserves the metadata for a specific chunk of output.
+type LogEntry struct {
+  // Data contains an unstructured byte array for the current entry from the process
+	Data      []byte
+  // Source is the type of output log from the process
+	Source    OutputSource
+  // Timestamp is the timestamp of the Capture event for this log
+	Timestamp time.Time
+}
+
+// OutputBuffer implements a thread-safe, multi-consumer broadcaster for process output
+type OutputBuffer struct {
+	sync.RWMutex
+	// cond is a condition variable used to wake up dormant client streamers when new data arrives.
+	cond *sync.Cond
+	// entries is the in-memory store of all stdout/stderr produced by the process.
+  entries []LogEntry
+	// closed indicates the process has finished writing to the buffer.
+	closed bool
+}

+type JobStatus int32
+
+const (
+  // StatusUnspecified indicates the status is unspecified
+  StatusUnspecified JobStatus = 0
+  // StatusRunning indicates the process has started and is currently active.
+	StatusRunning     JobStatus = 1
+  // StatusStopped indicates the process was manually terminated by a user request.
+	StatusStopped     JobStatus = 2
+  // StatusCompleted indicates the process exited on its own with a zero exit code.
+	StatusCompleted   JobStatus = 3
+  // StatusFailed indicates the process exited with a non-zero exit code or system error.
+	StatusFailed      JobStatus = 4

+// ExecutionSpecs defines the parameters provided by the client when a job is first created.
+type ExecutionSpecs struct {
+	// Command is the path to the executable to be run.
+	Command string
+  // Arguments is the path to the executable to be run.
+	Arguments []string
+	// OwnerCommonName is the Common Name extracted from the client's TLS certificate, used for ownership-based authorization.
+	OwnerCommonName string
+}

+// ResourceLimits defines the kernel-level constraints applied to a job.
+// These are implemented via Cgroups on Linux.
+type ResourceLimits struct {
+	// MemoryLimitBytes is the maximum physical memory the process tree can consume.
+	MemoryLimitBytes int64
+	// CPULimitPercent is the maximum CPU usage allowed (e.g., 0.5 for 50% of a core).
+	CPULimitPercent float64
+  // IOLimit is the maximum IO Read and Write for the process. It Requires specific properties to generate a string necessary for linux CGroup limits
+	IOLimit LinuxIOLimit
+}

+// IOLimit is the spec needed to generate a structured string for the linux cgroup.
+type LinuxIOLimit struct {
+    Major      int
+    Minor      int
+    ReadBPS    uint64
+    WriteBPS  uint32

+}

+    return nil
